body:
Part of #2607 (slice S2 of 6).

The order of the maintainer (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority".

## What
Add the GPU material removal kernel to `camcraft-gpu` (the crate of #2620).

- One invocation for each cell, for each batch of moves.
- The cut is `atomicMax` on the order-preserving u32 map of the S1 twin (#2626).
- Ball and upright flat end mills on linear moves only. Other kinds refuse by name, and the CPU cuts them.
- A dense lattice within `MAX_TEXELS`. The output layout is the `pack_cut` layout, so that `crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl` can read it.
- The kernel takes the device and queue that the caller gives.
- Limit the dispatch size to stay far below the Windows TDR (2 s). On an error, return `Err`. The caller runs the CPU path.

## Tests
- Parity on the software adapter (`headless_gpu` policy of #2620) against the S1 CPU twin:
  - bit equal on the same adapter in two runs;
  - one-sided against the f64 `field_cut` result.
- With no adapter: a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` makes it a failure (#615).
- Measure the time for one batch on the software adapter, and write it in the PR.

## Decision entry
A `docs/decisions/` entry for the `camcraft-gpu -> camcraft-sim` edge is necessary (AGENTS.md "No new dependency between our crates without a decision"). It lists the imported items: the sweep and tool data, the lattice meta, `CutPatch`, the pack functions.

## Prime Directive
No verdict, post gate or posted G-code reads this kernel. It is display only.

Blocked by #2626 (S1) and #2620 (the device home).

Done means: the kernel is in `camcraft-gpu` with the decision entry, and the parity tests are green on the software adapter.
